chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Rayyān that he said:

I wrote to al-Māḍī al-Ākhir عليه السلام asking him about a man who prayed two rakʿahs of the Salat of Jaʿfar, then a need hastened him away from the final two rakʿahs, or he cut that off due to an occurring incident. Is it permissible for him to complete it after finishing his need, even if he has risen from his place, or is that not counted for him unless he restarts the salat (prayer) and prays all four rakʿahs together in a single place?
So he عليه السلام wrote: “Yes. If a matter that he cannot do without interrupts him from that, then let him stop, then let him return and build upon what remains of it, if Allah wills.”

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer already performed
key_terms.صَلَاةِ جَعْفَرٍ: the devotional prayer of Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib
key_terms.فَلْيَبْنِ: let him continue on the basis of what he has already completed
key_terms.يَسْتَأْنِفَ: to begin the prayer anew from the start

ai.seo_question: Can someone resume Salat of Jaʿfar after interrupting it for a necessary reason?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about Salat of Jaʿfar when a necessary interruption occurs after two rakʿahs. It states that if the interruption is due to an unavoidable matter, the person may return later and complete what remains rather than restarting the entire prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1538 - It is narrated from Ali ibn al-Rayan that He said:

I wrote to the Last Imam (as) asking about a man who prayed two rak'ahs of the Salat of Ja'far but was forced to interrupt before completing the final two rak'ahs due to a need or an event that occurred. Would it be permissible for him to complete the remaining rak'ahs once his need was met, even if he had left his original place of prayer, or must he start the prayer again and pray all four rak'ahs together without interruption?
He (as) replied: "Yes, if he was interrupted by a matter of necessity, then let him stop and afterward return to complete what remains, if Allah (swt) wills."
